content.abbreviations: ACE-I = angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor; HFrEF = heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; LVEF = left ventricular ejection fraction; MRA = mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; NYHA = New York Heart Association; ARNI = angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor; NP = natriuretic peptide.
content.general_notes: a = Class of recommendation. b = Level of evidence.
content.5.3.1 Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhi: ACE-Is were the first drug class shown to reduce mortality and morbidity in patients with HFrEF and also improve symptoms. They are recommended for all patients unless contraindicated or not tolerated and should be uptitrated to the maximum tolerated recommended doses. Practical guidance referenced in Supplementary Table 2.
content.5.3.2 Beta-blockers: Beta-blockers reduce mortality and morbidity in HFrEF, in addition to treatment with an ACE-I and diuretic, and also improve symptoms. ACE-Is and beta-blockers can be commenced together as soon as symptomatic HFrEF is diagnosed; no evidence favors starting one before the other. Initiate in clinically stable, euvolemic patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually. In acute heart failure (AHF) admitted patients, start cautiously in hospital once hemodynamically stabilized. An IPD meta-analysis showed no benefit on hospital admissions and mortality in the subgroup of HFrEF patients with atrial fibrillation; guideline committee made no separate rhythm-based recommendation. Practical guidance referenced in Supplementary Table 3.
content.5.3.3 Mineralocorticoid receptor antagon: MRAs (spironolactone or eplerenone) are recommended in addition to an ACE-I and a beta-blocker in all patients with HFrEF to reduce mortality and risk of HF hospitalization and to improve symptoms. MRAs block aldosterone receptors and may also affect other steroid hormone receptors; eplerenone is more specific for aldosterone blockade and causes less gynaecomastia. Use caution with impaired renal function and when serum potassium >5.0 mmol/L. Practical guidance referenced in Supplementary Table 4.
content.5.3.4 Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin in: In the PARADIGM-HF trial, the ARNI sacubitril/valsartan was superior to enalapril in reducing hospitalizations for worsening HF, cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality in ambulatory HFrEF patients with LVEF ≤40% (later amended to ≤35% during the study). Patients in the trial had elevated plasma natriuretic peptide concentrations.
